Hi Jordan / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about Acme's fraud-detection workflow and the specific bottlenecks you mentioned (latency spikes at peak, false positives on certain vendor names, and the need for deterministic logs for audits). Below is a short recap and a proposed POC plan so we can confirm alignment before we draft the SOW.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: Reduce false positives on vendor name matching while keeping end-to-end inference latency under 150ms at 95th percentile.
- Secondary goals: Maintain or reduce per-request cost vs current baseline; produce auditable logs for each decision; ability to run in Acme's VPC (private deployment later).

Proposed POC scope and success criteria (draft)
1) Quality: Precision on flagged vendor-name matches >= 88% on your labeled holdout set (we'll work with the 2k-row file you mentioned).
2) Latency: 95th-percentile tail latency < 150ms under a representative shadow traffic profile (we'll define traffic shape).
3) Reliability / logs: Per-request trace and decision metadata available to your SIEM; KV cache warmup behavior documented.
4) Cost: Token cost + infra amortized at or below your target (TBD in SOW).

High-level timeline
- Kickoff & data handoff: target week of June 29 (please confirm availability).
- Evaluation: 2-3 weeks of offline testing + 1 week of online shadowing / soak.
- Review & decision: 1 week to iterate on remediations and sign-off.

Ownership / next steps
- Marissa (me) — overall program owner / commercial point of contact.
- Rachel Kim — evaluation methodology and labeling coordination (cc'd).
- Vivek — infra/ops lead for private deployment / VPC questions.

Attachments: POC-Statement-of-Work.pdf (draft), Acme-Eval-Rubric.xlsx (template).

Can you confirm the proposed success criteria above and whether the June 29 kickoff window works? If yes I will circulate a short SOW + meeting invite.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks, that all makes sense. Short answers inline: 

1) Yes — use the 2k as the primary holdout for acceptance. The 500-row international edge-case set is ideal as a challenge set during the "online shadow" phase and for targeted remediation.

2) Offline testing = batch evaluation on labeled sets (we run the eval harness against your holdout sets, measure precision/recall, hallucination checks, and run the rubric). Online shadowing = routing a copy of live traffic through the Redwood runtime in shadow mode so you can observe latency, throughput, cache behavior and live error modes without affecting production decisions. The two are complementary; offline verifies base quality, shadow validates infra behavior and integration.

3) Understood on procurement — I'll include clear acceptance thresholds and a pricing appendix in the SOW. I'll also pull in a short runbook for QoS tests.

Subject: Eval methodology + proposed grading rubric (Acme POC)

Hi all —

Following Marissa's ask, here's a concise eval plan and grading rubric we can use during the kickoff. Happy to iterate on Monday.

High-level approach
- Phase 1 (offline): Run automated evals against your labeled holdout (2k) and edge-case challenge (500). Metrics captured: precision, recall, F1; semantic similarity (embedding-based) for fuzzy matches; hallucination rate (manual spot check + detector); and per-row cost estimate.
- Phase 2 (shadow, online): Shadow live traffic for 5-7 days with traffic shape matched to your peak window. Capture: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit ratio, memory/KV cache warmup curves, error/retry rates, and end-to-end throughput under concurrency.

Suggested acceptance thresholds (draft)
- Precision (vendor-name flagged true positives) >= 88% on 2k holdout.
- Hallucination rate < 2% (as measured by our detector + manual review sampling).
- Tail latency (p95) < 150ms during shadow for representative traffic.

Grading rubric (sample)
- Column: Test / Metric | Scale 1-5 (1 = fail, 5 = meets/exceeds) | Notes
- Correctness (holdout set precision) | 1-5 | 5 if >= 88%, 3 if 75-87%, 1 if < 75%
- Edge-case robustness (500-row challenge) | 1-5 | 5 if edge false positives <= 5%, etc.
- Latency (p95) | 1-5 | 5 if <150ms, 3 if 150-250ms, 1 if >250ms
- Observability / logs | 1-5 | 5 if per-request trace + metadata available to SIEM
- Cost estimate | 1-5 | 5 if cost <= target; 3 if within 20%

Ownership and artifacts
- Redwood: run eval harness, provide results sheet (CSV), example queries that failed, deployment config for shadowing, and a remediation list.
- Acme: provide labeled holdout + challenge sets; a contact for data access; signoff on acceptance thresholds.

Runbook for online shadowing (short)
- Step 0: Agree on traffic window and allowlist (Vivek / Acme infra).
- Step 1: Start shadowing at 20% of peak traffic for 24h, inspect logs.
- Step 2: Ramp to 100% shadow for 5 days, capture p95/p99 and cache metrics.
- Step 3: Joint review and grade against rubric.

Attachments: Eval-Rubric-Sample.xlsx (simple scoring template).

Next steps before kickoff
- Acme: confirm labels/datasets transfer method and procurement contact for NDA/SOW (Marco).
- Redwood: finalize SOW with acceptance thresholds and draft pricing appendix; circulate calendar invite for June 29, 2pm PST.

I'll bring a sample notebook and the harness runbook to the kickoff so we can walk through an offline run start-to-finish.

Thanks,
